clickhouse.note: January 2026 Series D, $15B headline. The filing marks Nebius's securities at $1,518M after an option-pricing allocation and a 22.5% illiquidity discount. $2,000M is that allocation before the discount. A 25-28% times $15B stake (about $4B) is not the method in the filing, and there has been no round since.

toloka.note: 81% economic interest and 49% of the vote since the May 2025 round led by Bezos Expeditions. Nebius fair-valued the retained stake at $131M then. Books are $87M at June 30, 2026, after losses consumed the common. No later round. Community write-ups use roughly $300-500M.

otherBusinesses.note: No priced round, so this stays at zero. statements.text: Operated at peak utilization and were sold out of capacity in Q4 2025.
Expect to significantly increase capacity in place in Q3; majority of 2026 capacity comes online in the second half.
All capacity tranches delivered to Microsoft, including two in the past month. Plan to deploy more than 1 GW per year starting 2027.

Short-term capacity sells at $40–50M per MW per year versus $20–25M for 1–3 year deals; the first capacity auction cleared 15% above the previous top Blackwell price. Customer prepayments expected to exceed $9B in 2026. A Vineland site hearing was adjourned without a vote.

contracts.status: Delivery from early 2027. $12B dedicated; Meta to buy up to $15B more of capacity third parties don't take
Signed Q2 2026; average TCV >$1B, $20-25M per MW per year

backlog.note: About $40B of committed customer backlog, cited on the Q2 2026 call (from an AI-assisted transcript; not stated in the letter).

power.latestSecuredNote: Last disclosed secured figure. The Aug 2026 letter raised the year-end target to 5 GW ("we continue to secure power ahead of our expectations") without updating the secured-to-date number.

sentences: • The pace in which we bring capacity to market will accelerate as we plan to deploy more than 1 GW per year — and we plan to do so starting in 2027.
We now anticipate ending 2026 with 5 GW of contracted power(5), up from the +4 GW we indicated last quarter.
The pace at which we bring capacity to market will accelerate as we plan to deploy more than 1 GW per year, starting in 2027.
Nebius today also announced that it has secured up to 1.2 GW of power and land for a new, owned AI factory at a site in Pennsylvania.
• Owned capacity continues to expand rapidly Contracted capacity already exceeds 3.5 GW, far surpassing the goal of 3 GW we set for the end of the year.
We broke ground at our Missouri location yesterday; today, we are announcing a new site in Pennsylvania where we have secured power for a deployment of up to 1.2 GW.
We continue to expect 800MW to 1GW of connected power by year-end.

The planned AI factory at this location will be delivered in phases beginning in 2027 and will add to Nebius’s rapidly expanding US footprint, alongside the 1.2 GW AI factory in Independence, Missouri.
In the quarter we also announced a new owned location in Finland that when fully deployed at 310 MW will be one of Europe’s larg-est dedicated AI factories.
This led us to surpass our 2026 year-end contracted power target of 3 GW.
Our contracted capacity now exceeds 3.5 GW, with owned capacity representing more than 75% of the total.
Given this momentum, we are raising our contracted power guidance to more than 4 GW by year-end, with any additional contracts contributing to capacity growth in 2027 and beyond.
In total, our owned facilities will deliver 3 GW of capacity across five sites, reinforcing our commitment to a capital-efficient mod-el with attractive long-term unit economics.
● Capacity delivery ahead of plan ○ We ended the year with ~170MW of active power, vs our target of 100MW.
○ We have already secured more than 2 GW of contracted power, putting us well ahead of the target we set in November of more than 2.5 GW by the end of 2026.
As a result, we now expect to have more than 3 GW of contracted power by year-end .
We ended the year with ~170 MW of active power, significantly exceeding our 100 MW target.
We have made a strong start to our 2026 capacity plans, with today’s announcement of 9 new sites across the US and EMEA, already giving us a total of more than 2 GW of contracted power.
With our head start in securing power, we now expect to have more than 3GW of contracted power by the end of 2026 , up from our previous >2.5 GW target.
As we work to bring this capacity online, we also enter 2026 with strengthened conviction in achieving our 800MW to 1GW of connected power by the end of this year.
We are confident in our ability to deliver on our increased target for greater than 3 GW of contracted power by the end of 2026, having already secured more than 2 GW of contracted power to date.
